title: RCPC representation — action vocabulary
description:
The action vocabulary's metaschema. An action carries identity, parameters, parameter value schemas, and required capability types; `additionalProperties: false` admits nothing else. The instances live in `actions.json`, which validates against `#/$defs/actions_payload`; this file declares no instances. The planning and execution representations are generated from those definitions.

An action is declared once it has a real executor. Adding an action or a parameter type is an additive minor; removing one, or changing an action's parameters, is a major. See representation.md section 7.

action_id.title: Action identifier
action_id.description: The action's identity. Travels unchanged to the wire as the Behavior Tree node's registration name and the transport's `command`; no component maps it to a second token.

parameter_name.title: Parameter name
parameter_name.description: The role the parameter plays in the action, such as `target` or `object`. The execution projection rules map it to a Behavior Tree port name.

parameter.title: One parameter of an action
parameter.description: A name (the key) and a value schema (this object). `value` is a JSON Schema, not the name of one: declaring `target` as `common.schema.json#/$defs/position` says a supplied target is a position, and `validate.py` checks each supplied value against it. There is no separate type vocabulary.

value.title: The schema a supplied value must satisfy
value.description: A JSON Schema, in practice a `$ref` into `common.schema.json`, so a parameter's value and the product field holding the same kind of fact resolve to one definition. `common.schema.json#/$defs/robot_id` is excluded: no parameter may take a concrete robot as its value, because an action states the capability it requires and the robot is matched at dispatch. The `not` clause below is a shallow guard against a literal top-level `$ref` only; it is not authoritative. `validate.py` walks the whole value schema and is the check that holds for any indirection, such as an `allOf`-wrapped reference.

description.description: The parameter's role, for a human reader. Read by no component.

primitive_action.title: One action definition
primitive_action.description: Identity, parameters, required capability types, and a description. `additionalProperties: false` rejects any further field.

parameters.title: The action's parameters and the values they take
parameters.description: The action's arity and roles, each parameter carrying the schema its value must satisfy: `Attach(object, target)`, where `object` is an element identifier and `target` a position. A task instance supplies values for exactly these. Unordered; an action with no parameters declares an empty object.

requires_capabilities.title: The capability types this action requires
requires_capabilities.description: What a robot must offer to perform this action, by identifier from the capability vocabulary.

description.description: What the action does, for a human reader. Read by no component; states no precondition and no effect.

compound_id.title: Compound identifier
compound_id.description: The compound's identity. Unlike an action identifier it does not travel to the wire: a compound is never dispatched. It is how a plan's compound task names what it is, and how a method names what it requires.

compound_action.title: One compound definition
compound_action.description: Identity, an ordered decomposition, and a description. A compound itself does not perform an action, so it has no `parameters` and no `requires_capabilities`. `additionalProperties: false` rejects any further field.

decomposition.title: What this compound decomposes into, in order
decomposition.description: The actions the compound is made of, in the order they are performed. Repetition is meaningful, so `uniqueItems` is absent: `TransportComponent` names `MoveTo` twice. `minItems: 2`, because a body of one states no ordering and is a renaming of its single child.

items.description: One action in this compound's ordered decomposition, by identifier.

description.description: What the compound is, for a human reader. Read by no component; states no precondition and no effect.

actions_payload.title: query-representation, scope = actions
actions_payload.description: The `actions` query scope: the whole action vocabulary, as served. The referent of the `action` field every process-side task node carries, and of the `compound_name` a compound task carries. `compounds` is optional. `actions.json` is the instance this schema governs.

compounds.description: The compound definitions. Absent means the vocabulary declares none, not that they are declared elsewhere.

description.description: Optional annotation. Present on `actions.json`; a served payload omits it.
